messages:
Luisa M: FYI — Customer (AcmePayments) opened a ticket: streaming tool-call args are arriving truncated on our runtime, causing schema validation failures. Example payload we received (cut mid-array):
```json
{
  \"tool\": \"create_payment\",
  \"args\": {
    \"order_id\": \"ord_123456\",
    \"items\": [
      {\"sku\": \"sku-1\", \"qty\": 1},
      {\"sku\": \"sku-2\", \"qty\": 2},
      {\"sku\": \"sku-3\", \"qty\": 1}
    \"  <-- stream ended here (no closing ] or })
````
They get an InvalidToolArgs / JSON parse error. Customer says it happens ~1-2% of streams, intermittent.

Sam C: Can you paste the root request headers + model + SDK version + whether they're behind a proxy or CDN? Also the request-id from our runtime logs.

Luisa M: Sure — model: redwood/gpt-4x-infer, SDK: js@0.18.2, using our hosted API via customer's Fastly edge + our gateway. Request ID: req_0a9b3f4c. Request headers snippet: 
```
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
Accept: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive
User-Agent: acme-payments/1.4
```
Curl they used to reproduce (customer-provided):
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=redwood/gpt-4x-infer" \
  --data-binary @prompt.json
```

Keiko H: Oncall — intermittent SSE chunk splits look like this. Do we have runtime logs showing the exact byte frames? The InvalidToolArgs should include the truncated payload in the trace. Any proxy logs from Fastly?

Luisa M: I grabbed the runtime snippet from req_0a9b3f4c: 
```
ERROR runtime/parser.go:213 InvalidToolArgs: unexpected end of JSON input while parsing array
raw_stream_tail: '..., \"qty\": 1},
      {\"sku\": \"sku-3\", \"qty\": 1}
    ' (no closing tokens)
```
Fastly logs show re-chunking events aligned with connection resets.

Jamal R: Likely cause: CDN/proxy is re-chunking SSE chunks so a JSON object/array boundary is split across TCP segments; our parser assumes whole-tool-call JSON appears inside one SSE event. Two options:
1) Quick workaround for customer: disable streaming for tool calls or use direct connection (bypass Fastly) to confirm.
2) Proxy config mitigation: disable buffering/re-chunking. For nginx/edge snippets — ask customer to set on their edge if configurable: 
```nginx
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
```
Also recommend preserving event boundaries client-side and ensuring `Accept: text/event-stream`.

Luisa M: Can we do anything server-side to be more tolerant? Customer needs a non-breaking workaround while they update edge config.

Jamal R: Longer term: we'll add incremental reassembly tolerant parsing in runtime (hold incoming text until JSON is balanced or a max delay) and emit partial debug events. Filed ENG ticket INF-9423 and added notes about heuristics and cost. Short term: ask customer to use non-streaming or set X-Accel-Buffering/no buffering. I also recommended trying a quick test using `--no-proxy` or curl directly to our origin to confirm.

Support Bot: Created ticket INF-9423 and linked to eng-runtime. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9423 (assigned eng-runtime).

Sam C: Marking as P2 for now, escalated to eng-runtime. Requesting pcap/SSE capture and upstream CDN logs from customer. I'll add a repro checklist to the ticket.

Luisa M: Thanks team — I'll share the proxy snippet and the temporary non-streaming workaround with the customer and ask for CDN logs + a pcap. Will update the ticket when I have more. /cc @Keiko H
